# Linear Algebra – Part 2

## Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors
- $A v = \lambda v$
- Eigenvalues: scale factors
- Eigenvectors: directions of stretch

## Spectral Decomposition
- Symmetric $A = Q \Lambda Q^T$
- Diagonalization simplifies computation

## Singular Value Decomposition (SVD)
- $M = U \Sigma V^T$
- Decomposes any matrix into rotations + scaling
- Basis for low-rank approximation

## PCA via SVD
- Project data onto directions of max variance
- Scores = UΣ, components = V
- Rank-k approximations for dimensionality reduction

## Least Squares & Projection
- Normal equations: $X^TX \beta = X^T y$
- Projection matrix: $P = X(X^TX)^{-1} X^T$
- Optional: QR decomposition for numerical stability
